title: Cell-5 Heading Followed by a Simple List

illustrates.quote: A list is not preceded by a blank line: a. When it follows a cell-5 or cell-7 heading.

blocks.features: Bold, indented heading (print cell-5 style) directly above the list, no blank line beneath it in print.
Five one-word vocabulary items, one per line, no bullets or numbers, plain roman lowercase.

print.surroundingText: Rule 8.3.3.b (top box line) and 8.3.3.c (directions) follow, each cross-referencing Sample 8-4 and Example 8-4 respectively.
print.printFeatures: Boxed illustration; bold indented heading immediately above five plain lowercase words, no rule line or extra spacing between heading and list.

braille.notes: Heading ',vocabul>y ,^ws' (Vocabulary Words) begins 4 blank cells in (cell-5 indent, margin 0 stripped from the .txt since this example has no fixed left margin of literal spaces, unlike Examples 8-1/8-2); it is immediately followed by the list with no intervening blank line, illustrating 8.3.3.a; a blank line (line 7, all 40 cells blank) follows the list, matching the general 8.3.2.a rule for the list's own end.

resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. Heading level: both A and B stored the raw cell-position "5"; re-derived directly from the source .txt (U+2800 count before ",vocabul>y ,^ws", line 5797) = 4 leading blank cells, i.e. cell-5, matching Emboss’s own heading-level convention (1=centred/2=cell-5/3=cell-7, per the section-4 precedent) as level 2 — confirmed by the source’s own title "Example 8-3: Cell-5 Heading Followed by a Simple List".
